about: Values the NFHL holds that the November 2024 Domain Tables Technical Reference does not list, common enough that the models accept them with a LegacyValueWarning. Not upstream: an observation, not a specification. Each entry is a value of one domain-bound field of one service layer, with its row count from the observed snapshot; a test asserts the list is exactly what the threshold selects from that snapshot.
rule: A value is common when at least one row in a thousand of its layer holds it (count / layer total >= threshold). Measured against the layer rather than the field, because most of these fields are empty on most rows, so a share of the populated rows would admit the text-encoded nulls (-9999 is 97% of populated AR_REVERT). The null encodings written as text ('-9999', '<Null>', lone spaces) are not vocabulary values and are never admitted here, whatever their count.
